results.label: this tree ships the clean-rep count (src/challenge.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the count is versioned and names its three criteria in order, as the recorded facts they are
the basis says it counts TRADES and never days, and that an empty day neither adds nor breaks
the scope says a refused entry leaves no trade row (so it is neither a rep nor a failure) and that no record is not a clean record
an unset start is `not_set`, a valid one is a real UTC day, and a corrupt one is `unusable` rather than silently replaced
an unset target is the DEFAULT 21, a valid one is used, and a corrupt one is `unusable` (never silently 21)
a target a caller wants to store is validated, not coerced: 3 and "3" pass, "seven"/0/1000/21.5 are refused with the module’s own code
a start must be a real UTC day, and clearing it is a distinct, explicit value
a trade that is plan-linked, checklist-clean and journalled on its own close day is a rep
a trade with NO plan link is not a rep, and each failing criterion is named rather than summarised
a plan link that points at somebody else’s strategy is NOT a plan link: ownership is re-read, never trusted from the row
a trade with NO recorded checklist is not a rep: no record is not a clean record
one FAILED checklist item is a recorded breach, and the count of recorded checks rides the verdict
a recorded decision NOT to honour the stop is a breach even when every check passed
a stop whose honour was never recorded is not a recorded breach — the criterion is literally `no_recorded_breach`
a hand-written `journal_reviewed_at` with no matching hash does NOT count: the app’s own acknowledgement cannot be forged by filling the column
the criterion is the CLOSE DAY, not merely a completed review: the same acknowledgement a day later completes the journal and still does not count
and it is the UTC day at BOTH ends: a close and an acknowledgement 30 minutes apart across midnight UTC are two different days
an OPEN trade is never a rep, whatever else it carries: the SAME row is a rep when closed and is not when open
the window holds the trades from the start day on, and a trade closed BEFORE the start day is excluded — not counted and not a failure
a day with no closed trade is simply absent: the run is over consecutive REPS, not consecutive days, and the payload says skipping days is permitted
the run is consecutive reps NEWEST first: a failure after a rep leaves the count intact and restarts only the run
and a failure OLDER than every rep does not break the run either: the run is scanned from the newest trade, not from the start day
but a failure in the MIDDLE does break the run while leaving the count: the two numbers measure different things
the oldest and newest counted reps are reported by their own close instants, and the count is a count of trades
a trade with no usable close clock is counted in `undated_closes` rather than guessed onto a day
open trades are excluded from the window AND reported, so an open position can never look like a failed rep
each failure is attributed to its OWN criterion, a trade may fail several, and the reasons add up per criterion
the trades with NO recorded checklist at all are counted by name, so the trader learns why they do not count
the journal criterion reports the waiting trades by the fields the APP ITSELF says are missing, in the app’s own words
the observed gap between the recorded close and the recorded acknowledgement is reported, median and worst, so the calendar proxy can be read for what it is
`remaining` counts down to the target and `beyond_target` counts past it, both null when the stored target is unusable
moving the target never moves the count: the same rows scored against 2 and against 30 report the same reps and the same run
the newest trades in the window are listed with their own verdict and reasons, counted or not
a bounded read says so: the truncation flag is reported rather than the old trades quietly disappearing
an UNSTARTED count reports `not_started` with `counted:null` — never zero reps — and says starting it is the trader’s own act
an unreadable count is UNKNOWN: `unavailable` with `counted:null`, never an empty challenge, and the default wording says so in as many words
both shapes are read-only with zero writes and no influence on any grade, cap, permission, guardrail decision or plan change
and the count is never joined to an outcome: `outcome_joined:false` with the sentence saying why the exercise counts a habit
the payload carries NO money figure anywhere: nothing named for P&L, profit, amount, equity or a goal — the only `money` word is the note saying there is none
an owner that is not a positive id is refused with the module’s own code before any read happens

scope: M115 pure: the clean-rep count, its criteria and its refusals: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
